additions.reason: Line 3 of the source text explicitly equates two phrases: 'וְהַיְנוּ רוּחַ פִּיו, רוּחַ מְמַלְּלָא'. The word 'וְהַיְנוּ' (meaning: that is, i.e.) is a standard identity/bechina marker. The Rebbe is explaining what the ruach d'Mashiach that hovers over the chidushei Torah is — it is the 'ruach piv' (breath of his mouth, citing Psalms 33) and the 'ruach memalela' (the speaking spirit). This establishes a bechina equivalence between רוּחַ פִּיו and רוּחַ מְמַלְּלָא as two names for the same spiritual reality — the breath-dimension of Mashiach that animates Torah novelties. Both terms are aspects of the Mashiach-spirit cluster and should be added to Package 1 as bechina-equivalent satellite concepts orbiting משיח.

The paired term with רוּחַ פִּיו (see above). The Zohar's description of the spirit of Mashiach that hovers over the waters (the Torah) is here identified as 'ruach memalela' — the speaking/articulating spirit. This is the Aramaic form of the same concept: the spiritual breath that gives voice to Torah insights, which is the animating force present in every chidush Torah. Since רוּחַ פִּיו and רוּחַ מְמַלְּלָא are given as co-equal definitions of the ruach d'Mashiach in this Torah, both should be added as bechina-satellite nodes in Package 1, forming a bechina edge between them and linking both to משיח.
